title: My first game failed successfully. Here's game #2
author: kutan74
selftext:
Still very early, but I've been working a cozy city-builder with traffic simulation, layered roads, buildings and a small living city feel. 

Would love to hear what you think of the direction so far.

comments.author: Grandrcp
comments.body: How did you create your assets, mainly buildings and people? I stuggle a lot with people animation

replies.author: kutan74
replies.body: I use Rodin AI to create models and mixamo for animations

replies.author: Prior-Meeting1645
replies.body: Is rodin same as meshy and tripo?

replies.author: Illustrious-Peanut77
replies.body:
I'm getting into game development using Ai but I'm struggling with the feeling that I haven't actually created anything as it's all been created by AI. I also get the same feeling when viewing other people's creations. It's like yeh that's cool but you actually didn't make any of that (no skill needed) AI did it for you. 

Personally I need that sense of "I actually made that" and because of this I'm struggling to enjoy using AI. 

Anybody else feel the same?

comments.author: SimCFB
comments.body: that looks fantastic. are you  modeling it after Sim City?

replies.author: kutan74
replies.body: Thanks! A little bit, yeah but I'm aiming for something smaller, cozier.

comments.author: Own-Floor3521
comments.body: woah the water looks really good. How did you do that?

replies.author: kutan74
replies.body: I used a custom water asset for this

comments.author: Icy-Revolution4717
comments.body: I have a dream of developing some kind of isometric game in a future too. Yours looks awesome. First thing that comes to mind by looking at that city is to make every person an Ai character. I would try to use that recently hyped  Ai program that can simulate a society where every ai has it's own character. And then just watch them evolve and see where it will take them. Have no idea if that's even possible but I think that would be a fun game.

replies.author: rapkannibale
replies.body: What is this AI program you mentioned?

replies.author: Icy-Revolution4717
replies.body: it's MiroFish. Not even sure if it can be used here. Just a thought outloud [GitHub - 666ghj/MiroFish: A Simple and Universal Swarm Intelligence Engine, Predicting Anything. 简洁通用的群体智能引擎，预测万物 · GitHub](https://github.com/666ghj/MiroFish)

comments.author: BlazyGameDev
comments.body: Did you use a building generator ? This looks interesting

replies.author: kutan74
replies.body: Thanks! Yeah some of the buildings are made with AI-assisted 3D tools, then I clean them up and integrate everything into Unreal

comments.author: trevormorrison123
comments.body: Love the "peaceful GTA" feel... what's the inner mechanisms, like e.g. does it route individual people to.. what... workplace or so?

replies.author: kutan74
replies.body: Yeah that's the idea. Citizens have homes/workplaces and actual commute routes, so building placement should directly affect traffic
